definitions.gloss: dengaku; miso-glazed grilled food on skewers
definitions.explanation: A traditional Japanese dish where tofu, eggplant, konnyaku, or other ingredients are skewered and grilled with a sweet miso glaze. Named after a traditional rice-planting dance because the skewered food resembles performers on stilts.

examples.japanese: {豆腐|とうふ}の{田楽|でんがく}を{作|つく}った。
{茄子|なす}の{田楽|でんがく}は{味噌|みそ}の{甘|あま}さが{絶品|ぜっぴん}だ。
examples.english: Eggplant dengaku is exquisite with the sweetness of the miso.

examples.japanese: {囲炉裏|いろり}のある{古民家|こみんか}で{食|た}べるこんにゃくの{田楽|でんがく}は{格別|かくべつ}だった。
examples.english: The konnyaku dengaku eaten at an old farmhouse with a traditional hearth was exceptionally good.

notes:
USAGE:
Usually preceded by the ingredient name: {豆腐|とうふ}{田楽|でんがく} (tofu dengaku), {茄子|なす}{田楽|でんがく} (eggplant dengaku), こんにゃく{田楽|でんがく} (konnyaku dengaku). The miso glaze can be white miso, red miso, or a blend, sometimes with added sweetness from sugar or mirin.

COMMON VARIETIES:
- {豆腐|とうふ}{田楽|でんがく}: grilled tofu with miso glaze (the classic version)
- {茄子|なす}{田楽|でんがく}: grilled eggplant with miso
- こんにゃく{田楽|でんがく}: grilled konnyaku with miso
- {里芋|さといも}{田楽|でんがく}: grilled taro with miso

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {田楽|でんがく}{味噌|みそ}: dengaku miso (the sweet miso glaze)
- {田楽|でんがく}を{焼|や}く: to grill dengaku
